correctness.rationale: Beta integral and recurrence reconstruct normalized cost. Exact sign factor H and its increasing ratio for alpha<1 give an exhaustive unique first crossing and all boundary ties; C(k)<1 for large k excludes singleton. Gamma asymptotics and uniform log expansion give k~1/alpha and two-term Cmin. Exact rational checks pass and their finite nature is explicitly limited.

originality.rationale: The novel assertion is not the beta-binomial zero-pool law known since Lendle et al. or the 2021 beta-binomial optimal-pool comparison. It is a complete unrestricted integer crossing classification in the low-shape regime and its fixed-correlation rare-prevalence inverse-p scaling with a two-term cost asymptotic. Primary full-text sections and generalized 2023 framework were compared by mathematical implication rather than by title; residual priority risk is explicit.

value.rationale: For fixed positive dependence, beta mixture produces an inverse-prevalence rather than inverse-square-root pooling scale, and a \(p\log(1/p)\) rather than sqrt(p) test-cost scale. This affects how correlated rare-infection screening models can be optimized, and the exact integer crossing rule is globally usable without numerical cutoff. No empirical or finite-cluster implementation claim is made.
